channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan payment organizations to issue stablecoins and handle cross-border transfers
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank will allow first-category payment organizations to issue stablecoins and service cross-border transfers. These organizations will gain direct access to payment systems and act as a regulated channel between the payment and digital asset markets. They will also be designated as currency control agents, subject to enhanced regulatory requirements.

item.title: Astana Company Denies Rumors of Apartment Building Demolition for LRT Project
item.description: City Transportation Systems (CTS) has denied information circulating on social media that an apartment building at 23 Kenesary Street in Astana will be demolished for the Light Rail Transit (LRT) line. Residents had expressed concern about potential demolition. CTS stated that the demolition of this specific residential building is not part of the LRT construction project plans.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Announces Increases in Social Payments, Salaries, and Pensions
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov informed residents of Manas city and Suzak district about upcoming increases in social benefits, salaries, and pensions. Starting January 1, 2027, disability benefits will rise to 11,000 soms, and payments for children who lost both parents will increase to 8,000 soms. Salary increases for educators and healthcare workers have already been implemented.

item.title: UN Confirms Security Incident Involving Staff Member in Bamiyan
item.description: The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) confirmed a security incident on October 21 in Bamiyan involving a staff member. Sources reported the UNAMA official's vehicle came under gunfire. UNAMA stated the staff member was unharmed and is gathering information. Images suggest damage to the vehicle.

item.title: Investor Receives Full Refund of Overpaid Value-Added Tax in Zhetysu Region
item.description: The Zhetysu Region prosecutor's office has recovered over 14.6 million tenge in value-added tax mistakenly paid by an investor. The prosecutor's office intervened after discovering the overpayment, ensuring the company's rights were restored and the funds were returned. The strategic industrial project continues without administrative barriers.

item.title: Reporters Without Borders Supports Kazakh Journalists' Demand for Access to Parliament
item.description: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) backs Kazakh journalists demanding the lifting of restrictions on their work within parliament. RSF calls for the immediate cancellation of new rules that have led to media warnings and denied accreditation. Forty journalists have appealed to the speaker to allow questions beyond the stated agenda, deeming current limitations unjustified.

item.title: Over 80 Percent of Dairy Products in Kyrgyzstan Imported from Russia and Belarus
item.description: Kyrgyzstan imports over 80 percent of its dairy products from Russia and Belarus, according to the National Statistical Committee. For January-August 2026, import volumes were 1.98 times higher than exports, driven by large-scale imports of foreign cheese, cottage cheese, and milk powder. Domestic dairy exports are declining.

item.title: Almaty Mart Mall Reports Significant Profit Drop in Q3 2026
item.description: The Almaty Mart Mall's real estate investment fund, Almaty Logistic Center (ALC), reported a profit of 704.3 million tenge for Q3 2026, a sharp decrease from 4.6 billion tenge in the same period of 2025. Revenue also fell to 1.3 billion tenge from 5.2 billion tenge. The fund's undistributed profit stood at 2.1 billion tenge as of September 30, 2026.

item.title: Trump: US Closer Than Ever to Resolving Russia-Ukraine Conflict
item.description: President Donald Trump stated that the resolution of the military conflict between Russia and Ukraine is closer than ever before. He mentioned speaking with Vladimir Putin about settling the war and believes a breakthrough is imminent. The US is reportedly ready to resume trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine in early November.

item.title: Teenager and Two Men Sentenced for Fatal Assault in Balkhash
item.description: A teenager and two men have been sentenced in the Karaganda region for beating a man to death in a hospital. The court considered the teenager's age as a mitigating factor but still ordered his imprisonment. The assault occurred on December 22, 2025, resulting in the victim's death from head injuries sustained during the fight.

item.title: One in Two Juvenile Crimes in Kazakhstan Classified as Serious or Especially Serious
item.description: Over the past three years, approximately 7,000 minors in Kazakhstan have committed crimes, with nearly half classified as serious or especially serious offenses. The Prosecutor General's Office reported a 7% decrease in juvenile crime. Initiatives like the BALAZHAN platform and the AiMap IT system are being implemented to identify and support at-risk children.

item.title: Astana Airport to Launch Facial Recognition for Domestic Flights Without Separate Funding
item.description: Astana Airport plans to implement facial recognition for domestic flight passengers, utilizing the eGov Mobile app for consent. The system will verify identity at security and boarding gates. No separate funding is allocated, and a mechanism for data deletion is not provided. Passengers can opt-out of the pilot project.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize 620 Saiga Horns Destined for China
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee reported that border guards at the "Khorgos" international border cooperation center intercepted an attempt to illegally export 620 saiga horns to China on October 20. The black market value of the horns is estimated at around 180 million tenge. The case materials have been transferred to the relevant authorities.

item.title: Bishkek extends leases for electric charging stations amid ongoing discussions
item.description: Bishkek's city council is reviewing and extending one-year leases for operational electric charging stations, provided there are no violations. This comes after numerous appeals from entrepreneurs. The municipality plans to install its own charging devices and sell electricity at cost, potentially eliminating the need for intermediaries.

item.title: Two-year-old dies after building facade collapses at Karaganda cultural center
item.description: A two-year-old child died after a facade from a cultural center building collapsed in the Karaganda region on April 13. Doctors attempted to save the child for three months. The child's parents had repeatedly requested the closure of the building due to potential safety concerns.

item.title: Alisher Kuchiyev Appointed Deputy Economic Policy Advisor to Uzbekistan President
item.description: Alisher Kuchiyev has been appointed as the Deputy Advisor on Economic Policy to the President of Uzbekistan. The decree was signed by Head of the Presidential Administration Saida Mirziyoyeva. Kuchiyev previously worked at the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank for over two years.

item.title: US Orders Non-Essential Personnel and Families to Leave Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks
item.description: The US State Department has ordered non-essential personnel and their families at the US Embassy in Saudi Arabia to leave the country. This decision follows deadly Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The safety of personnel is the highest priority, according to a State Department spokesperson.

item.title: Kaspi.kz Launches Service for Registration with Medical Organizations
item.description: Kaspi.kz has launched a new service allowing users to quickly and easily register with medical organizations via the Kaspi.kz app. This initiative, developed in cooperation with government bodies, aims to simplify daily tasks for citizens. The service allows remote selection of medical facilities.

item.title: Astana City Transportation Denies Claims of Demolishing Residential Building for LRT Construction
item.description: City Transportation Systems (CTS) in Astana has refuted claims that a residential building at Kensary Street 23 will be demolished for the construction of the Tarlan Astana light rail transit system. Residents had expressed shock over potential demolition, but CTS confirmed the project does not include the building's removal. The LRT system, launched on May 16, has served nearly 11.5 million passengers.

item.title: Over 20,000 Central Asians Recruited by Russia for War in Ukraine, Report Claims
item.description: A Ukrainian project, 'I Want to Live,' claims Russia has recruited 20,437 citizens from five Central Asian countries for the war in Ukraine since 2022, constituting 44% of identified foreign contract soldiers. Uzbekistan leads with 8,207, followed by Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkmenistan. The report notes a significant increase in recruitment in recent years.

item.title: Kazakh banks reduce deposit interest rates, impacting returns for savers
item.description: Kazakhstan's banks are lowering deposit interest rates, though some savings accounts still offer up to 19.5% annual effective yield. A major bank will adjust six-month deposit rates from 17.74% to 14.47% effective October 23, potentially reducing returns by approximately 15,000 tenge on a 1 million tenge deposit.

item.title: Osh residents debate demolition of family dormitories for new multi-story buildings
item.description: Negotiations are underway in Osh regarding the demolition of old family dormitories in the 'Manas-Ata' microdistrict to build multi-story housing. Residents, many of whom are vulnerable families, are concerned about relocation costs and the affordability of new apartments. The current buildings, constructed in the 1950s-1960s, are in poor condition.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Banking Sector: High Profits Amidst Rising Credit Costs and Delinquency
item.description: Despite banks in Kazakhstan earning trillions of tenge and becoming more technologically advanced, consumer loans remain expensive. Elena Bakhmutova, head of the Association of Financiers of Kazakhstan, discusses why banks are profitable while borrowers face high interest rates and increasing overdue debt. The article explores risks in installment purchases and the responsibility for fraudulent loans.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Nearly 7,000 Minors Committed Crimes in Past Three Years, Prosecutor General's Office Reports
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of Kazakhstan reported that approximately 7,000 minors committed crimes in the last three years, with nearly half classified as serious or particularly serious offenses. Around 2,500 teenagers have been convicted, and 3,000 are under police preventive watch. Over 800,000 children require assistance, with a new platform, BALAZHAN, launched to track their needs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Pledges Funds for Development in Manas and Suzak Districts
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited the Jalal-Abad region to review socio-economic development in Manas city and Suzak district. He was presented with development results and future plans. Significant infrastructure projects, including schools, roads, and healthcare facilities, are underway or completed. Investments are also being made in housing and commercial markets.

item.title: US Seeks to Reduce Reliance on China for Mineral Supplies, Eyes Central Asia
item.description: The US is seeking to diversify its supply of critical minerals, aiming to reduce dependence on China. Despite a trade truce extension, Washington remains concerned about China's export restrictions. China dominates global production and processing of these minerals, essential for various high-tech applications including electric vehicles and defense systems.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Mandatory Psychological Diagnostics for Educators and Students
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce mandatory psychological diagnostics for educators and students at least once per academic year. This initiative, starting in the 2026/2027 academic year for preschools and schools, and in 2027/2028 for vocational and higher education, aims to identify and support individuals needing psychological assistance. Results will be analyzed by AI to categorize individuals into 'psychologically stable,' 'needing support,' or 'requiring active support.'

item.title: New 220kV Power Substation to be Built in Dushanbe with Japanese Grant
item.description: Tajikistan and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have signed a grant agreement to construct a new 220/110/10 kV power substation in eastern Dushanbe. The project aims to strengthen the capital's energy infrastructure, enhance electricity supply reliability, and meet growing demand. This initiative is part of ongoing energy cooperation between Tajikistan and Japan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Otbasar Bank' and Ulytau Region to Allocate 3 Billion Tenge Annually for Housing
item.description: Kazakhstan's 'Otbasar Bank,' a subsidiary of 'Baiterek' Holding, and the Ulytau regional administration have signed a memorandum to jointly finance housing programs from 2027 to 2029. The bank will contribute 2.5 billion tenge annually, and the regional administration 500 million tenge, to provide affordable loans for residents. This aims to help locals purchase housing and settle in the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Offer Subsidies for Relocation to Labor-Short Regions Starting 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will offer subsidies to citizens relocating to one of seven designated labor-short regions. The program, part of the 'Rules for Voluntary Resettlement to Increase Labor Mobility,' is open to residents of regions with the fastest population growth over the last decade. Participants must secure employment or start a business in their new location.

item.title: Tajikistan's Mufti Urges Soldiers to Avoid Harming Comrades and Support Each Other
item.description: Amid ongoing army conscription in Tajikistan, marked by reluctance due to hazing and humiliation, the head of the Council of Ulemas urged servicemen to support one another. Saidmukarram Abdukodirzoda's appeal, made during a meeting with border troops, emphasized mutual respect, patience, and high moral principles, addressing persistent complaints of mistreatment.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Transition to Two-Stage Military Service Model
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning a military reform that includes restructuring forces, improving command and control, establishing drone units, and strengthening army components. A key aspect is a shift to a two-stage conscript service: six months of training followed by six months of operational duty in military units. Measures to ensure soldier safety and rights are also planned.

item.title: Red Cross Enhances Safe Drinking Water Access for 38,500 People in Herat's Gulran District
item.description: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has installed or repaired 275 water pumps in Gulran district, Herat province, improving access to safe drinking water for 38,500 residents. The initiative has also led to a decline in illnesses among locals.

item.title: Afghan Male University Enrollment Drops by One-Third Since 2019, Report Finds
item.description: A UNICEF and UNESCO report indicates a significant decline in Afghan male university enrollment, falling by approximately one-third from 306,000 in 2019 to 208,000 in 2026. Female enrollment has also drastically decreased, reaching zero since 2024. The report attributes this contraction to reduced household ability to pay, weaker employment prospects, and financial pressure on universities.

item.title: Industrial Park for Non-Ferrous Metals to Be Established in Northern Tajikistan
item.description: An industrial park for non-ferrous metals will be established in northern Tajikistan through cooperation between Tajikistan's Ministry of Industry, China's Non-Ferrous Metals Industry Association, and Tibet Everest Company. The collaboration aims to develop deep processing of mineral raw materials, increase added value, localize production, create jobs, and expand export capacity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Lawmakers Raise Corruption Concerns Over State Procurement Bill
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber debated a bill to allow state procurement to proceed even with a single supplier. Lawmakers voiced concerns about corruption risks and limited competition, leading to the bill's return for revision.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Warns US Against Further Military Attacks
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has warned the US against potential further attacks, stating Iran is prepared for diplomacy if trust is built. He cautioned that choosing war over diplomacy would lead to a significant strategic defeat for the US.

item.title: ADB Grants Tajikistan $63.77 Million for Healthcare and Social Insurance Projects
item.description: The government of Tajikistan and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) signed grant agreements for two projects totaling $63.77 million. The funds are allocated to strengthen the healthcare system and modernize social insurance. The first project receives $43.7 million for regional health security and primary care, while the second gets $20.5 million for social insurance digitalization.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Social Democrats Leader Demands Open Trial from Prison
item.description: Imprisoned Kyrgyz politician Temirlan Sultanbekov, leader of the Social Democrats party, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for an open trial regarding his case. Sultanbekov claims political motivation and alleges evidence tampering, specifically a manipulated video used against him. He emphasizes the public's right to witness court proceedings.

item.title: Kazakhstan Provides Clarifications on New QazETA Electronic Entry System to Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry stated that information on the QazETA electronic entry permit system has been sent to all affected countries, including Russia. This response addresses Moscow's request for clarification on new migration rules, which will apply to citizens of 85 countries.
